note: Beaumont-Port Arthur on the Neches with Jack Brooks airport; covers Port Arthur, Nederland, Orange and Vidor. The Sabine River state line is not the edge: Lake Charles, (LA), US meets it a few km inside Louisiana. Houston meets it west of Winnie.

note: Houston with Bush Intercontinental and Hobby; covers The Woodlands, Conroe, Katy, Sugar Land, Pearland, Baytown and Galveston Island. The coast and Galveston Bay bound the south-east; College Station takes the land north-west of Hempstead.

note: McAllen for the lower Rio Grande Valley: Edinburg, Mission, Pharr, Harlingen and Brownsville, with McAllen, Harlingen and Brownsville airports. The Rio Grande is a hard border with Reynosa and Matamoros, MX. South Padre Island is left out on purpose (Colin, 2026-10-14: materially distinct despite the causeway).

note: Southern San Joaquin Valley around Bakersfield (Meadows Field airport), with Delano, Wasco, Shafter, Arvin and Tehachapi. Fresno, (CA), US to the north, Santa Maria, (CA), US and Santa Barbara, (CA), US over the Coast Ranges, Los Angeles, (CA), US over the Tehachapi Mountains; the east reaches the Kern River valley and Mojave edge.

note: Northern Sacramento Valley around Chico (CIC airport) with Paradise, Oroville, Orland and Corning. Redding, (CA), US to the north and Sacramento, (CA), US to the south split the valley; the Sierra foothills and Feather River canyon close the east.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Fresno): 717,589; within 1.5x of p, stands
note: Central San Joaquin Valley: Fresno and Clovis (FAT airport), Visalia, Tulare, Hanford, Madera. The Sierra Nevada closes the east up to the 100 km arc; the Coast Ranges west of I-5 face Salinas, (CA), US. Staircase on the Salinas edge removed.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Indio-Palm Desert-Palm Springs): 361,075; proposed, more than 1.5x p
note: Coachella Valley: Indio, Palm Springs (PSP airport), Palm Desert, La Quinta, Cathedral City, plus Twentynine Palms and the Salton Sea. San Jacinto and Santa Rosa mountains separate it from Riverside, (CA), US; the east is empty Colorado Desert along I-10.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim): 12,237,376; proposed, more than 1.5x p
note: Los Angeles County and Orange County: LAX, Burbank, Long Beach and John Wayne airports, Santa Clarita, Lancaster-Palmdale, Thousand Oaks. Santa Ana Mountains and the LA/San Bernardino county line divide it from Riverside, (CA), US; Catalina is included as near-shore.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Modesto): 357,301; proposed, more than 1.5x p
note: Northern San Joaquin Valley: Modesto, Stockton (SCK airport), Tracy, Manteca, Turlock, Merced, Patterson, Los Banos. The west edge follows the Diablo Range foothills; the empty range beyond is in no city. The Altamont hills separate it from San Francisco, (CA), US.

note: Western Inland Empire: Riverside, Ontario (ONT airport), Rancho Cucamonga, Upland, Chino, Corona, Moreno Valley, Temecula, Murrieta. Santa Ana Mountains to the west, the county line with San Bernardino, (CA), US to the north.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Sacramento): 1,946,618; proposed, more than 1.5x p
note: Sacramento Valley around the state capital (SMF airport): Elk Grove, Roseville, Folsom, Davis, Vacaville, Woodland. Reaches the Sierra foothills toward Lake Tahoe, where Reno, (NV), US takes over; Fairfield goes whole to San Francisco, (CA), US.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Salinas): 177,532; within 1.5x of p, stands
note: Monterey Bay: Salinas, Monterey (MRY airport), Santa Cruz, Watsonville, Gilroy, Hollister, Morgan Hill. Santa Cruz Mountains face Silicon Valley, (CA), US; the Diablo Range faces Fresno, (CA), US. The sea corner shared with San Francisco was pulled in from 111 km.

p_note: 2020 Census Riverside-San Bernardino urban area 2,276,703 is shared by two mapped cities; city figure kept to avoid counting it twice (question for Colin)
note: Eastern Inland Empire: San Bernardino, Fontana, Rialto, Colton, Redlands, Yucaipa, Highland, the I-15 corridor through Devore and Cajon Pass to the Victor Valley, plus Big Bear. The line with Riverside, (CA), US follows the county line.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (San Diego): 3,070,300; proposed, more than 1.5x p
note: San Diego County west of the mountains: San Diego (SAN airport), Chula Vista, Oceanside, Escondido, Carlsbad, El Cajon. The Mexican border is hard (Tijuana, MX is separate); Camp Pendleton separates it from Orange County; the Laguna Mountains from Indio, (CA), US.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (San Francisco-Oakland): 3,515,933; proposed, more than 1.5x p
note: Bay Area outside Silicon Valley: San Francisco (SFO), Oakland (OAK), Berkeley, Hayward, Walnut Creek, the north Peninsula, Marin, Vallejo, Napa and Fairfield. Silicon Valley, (CA), US takes the south Bay from San Mateo down; the sea corner reach drops from 114 km to 108 km.

note: Hand-painted: San Jose (SJC airport), Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Redwood City, Fremont, Milpitas. Only edges refined: the San Mateo line runs through the San Mateo/Foster City overlap; Union City goes whole to it.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Santa Barbara): 202,197; proposed, more than 1.5x p
note: South coast and Ventura County: Santa Barbara (SBA airport), Goleta, Carpinteria, Ventura, Oxnard, Port Hueneme. Santa Ynez Mountains behind; the line with Los Angeles, (CA), US runs between Oxnard and Camarillo, now clear of Oxnard.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Santa Maria): 143,609; within 1.5x of p, stands
note: Central coast: Santa Maria, San Luis Obispo (SBP airport), Lompoc, Arroyo Grande, Atascadero, Paso Robles. The Santa Ynez Valley divides it from Santa Barbara, (CA), US; the Temblor Range from Bakersfield, (CA), US.

note: San Angelo with Goodfellow AFB and Mathis Field; covers Ballinger, Eden and Eldorado. Abilene and Midland meet it to the north; the rest is the 100 km arc over the Edwards Plateau ranch land.

note: Upper Sacramento Valley: Redding (RDD airport), Anderson, Shasta Lake, Red Bluff, and I-5 north to Mount Shasta. Klamath Mountains west, Lassen and Cascades east; Medford, (OR), US beyond the Siskiyous.

note: Puget Sound: Seattle (SEA airport), Tacoma, Bellevue, Everett, Olympia, Bremerton, Kitsap and Whidbey Island. Cascade crest to the east (Snoqualmie Pass), the Olympic Mountains to the west; Bellingham and the Olympic Peninsula coast are outside.

note: Inland Northwest: Spokane (GEG airport), Spokane Valley, Cheney, and Coeur d'Alene, Post Falls and Hayden in Idaho. Palouse farmland south toward Lewiston, (ID), US; Garfield now whole in Spokane.

p_note: 2020 US Census urban area (Yakima): 133,145; within 1.5x of p, stands
note: Yakima Valley: Yakima (YKM airport), Selah, Union Gap, Toppenish, Sunnyside, Ellensburg, and Wenatchee near the 100 km arc. Cascade crest separates it from Seattle, (WA), US; Kennewick, (WA), US takes the lower valley from Prosser.
